'''John Dudley Corbett''' (March 23, 1926 – September 2, 2013) was an American chemist who specialized in [[inorganic]] [[solid-state chemistry]].  At Iowa State and Ames Lab, Corbett lead a research group that focused on the synthesis and characterization of two broad classes of materials, notably [[Zintl phases]]<ref>Multiple sources:

*{{Cite journal|last1=Henning|first1=Robert|last2=Leon-Escamilla|first2=E.A.| last3=Zhao|first3=Jing-Tai| last4=Corbett|first4=John D.|date=1997|title=Stabilization by Hydrogen. Synthetic and Structural Studies of the Zintl Phase Ba5Ga6H2|journal=Inorganic Chemistry|volume=36|issue=7|pages=1282–1285|doi=10.1021/ic9612966|pmid=11669703}}
*{{Cite journal|last1=Mudring|first1=A.V.|last2=Corbett|first2=John D.|date=2004|title=Unusual electronic and bonding properties of the Zintl phase Ca5Ge3 and related compounds. A Zintl Phase with a Helical Framework Structure|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |volume=118|issue=48|pages=12098–12103|doi=10.1021/ja961975f}}</ref> and condensed transition metal == Career ==
After graduating from [[Yakima High School]], serving in the [[United States Navy]] until the end of [[World War II]], and attending the [[Valley City State University|North Dakota Teachers College]], the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], and the [[University of Washington]], Corbett remained at Washington to complete his Ph.D. in 1952.<ref name="journalobit"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Svec |first1=Kathy |title=Corbett, John Dudley |url=https://isubios.pubpub.org/pub/18br5qoa/release/1 |access-date=August 6, 2023 |publisher=Iowa State University |date=July 30, 2021}}</ref> He joined the chemistry faculty of [[Iowa State University]] and the scientific staff of [[Ames Laboratory]] in 1953.  He was affiliated with both institutions for his entire career, and served as chair of the Department of Chemistry between 1968 and 1973.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Kauzlarich |first1=Susan M. |author1-link=Susan M. Kauzlarich |title=Obituary: John D. Corbett (1926–2013) |journal=Comments on Inorganic Chemistry |date=2014 |volume=34 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–2 |doi=10.1080/02603594.2013.867404|s2cid=98454192 }}</ref> He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]. He was awarded two DOE Awards for Outstanding Scientific Accomplishments and Sustained Research in Materials Chemistry, the [[Humboldt Prize]] (1985), the 2005 [[Frank Spedding|Spedding]] Award from the Rare Earth Research Conference,<ref>{{cite news |title=Ames Laboratory's John Corbett wins Spedding award |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/715612 |access-date=August 6, 2023 |publisher=EurekAlert! |date=March 9, 2005}}</ref> the 2008 Monie A. Ferst Award from [[Sigma Xi]], and several ACS Awards for both [[Inorganic Chemistry]] and Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Inorganic Chemistry.<ref name="isuobit">{{Cite web |url=http://www.chem.iastate.edu/faculty/John_Corbett/ |title=John D. Corbett &#124; Department of Chemistry |access-date=2011-11-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707081046/https://www.chem.iastate.edu/faculty/John_Corbett |archive-date=2018-07-07 |url-status=dead }} [https://www.chem.iastate.edu/people/john-corbett Alternate URL]</ref> He was elected to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1992.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mcbmm.ameslab.gov/org_john_corbett.htm |title=Materials Chemistry and Biomolecular Materials at Ames Laboratory |accessdate=2011-11-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425235715/http://www.mcbmm.ameslab.gov/org_john_corbett.htm |archivedate=2012-04-25 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=John D. Corbett |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/john-d-corbett-sfmynd/ |access-date=August 6, 2023 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Corbett was born to parents Alexander and Elizabeth Corbett in [[Yakima, Washington]], on March 23, 1926, and had two brothers. He was married to F. Irene Lienkaemper from 1948 until her death in 1996.<ref>{{cite news |title=John D. Corbett |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/92/i18/John-D-Corbett.html |access-date=August 6, 2023 |work=C&EN |date=May 5, 2014}}</ref> The couple raised three children. Corbett died on September 2, 2013, at the age of 87, following a stroke.<ref name="isuobit"/><ref name="journalobit">{{cite journal |last1=Meyer |first1=Gerd |last2=Mudring |first2=Anja-Verena |last3=Poeppelmeier |first3=Kenneth R. |title=John D. Corbett (1926–2013) |journal=Angewandte Chemie |date=2013 |volume=52 |pages=113513–113514 |doi=10.1002/anie.201309705}}</ref> The John D. Corbett Professorship was established in 2007, within Iowa State University's Department of Chemistry.<ref name="isuobit"/><ref>{{cite news |title=John Corbett, longtime ISU chemistry professor, passes away |url=https://archive.las.iastate.edu/2013/09/04/john-corbett-longtime-isu-chemistry-professor-passes-away/ |access-date=August 6, 2023 |publisher=Iowa State University College of Liberals Arts and Sciences |date=September 4, 2013}}</ref>
